tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: M2 label detection conflates firm-name outlines in title blocks, callout annotations, and room labels. M3 needs a classification pass: title-block exclusion zone (border region = firm name noise), leader-line proximity detection (callouts), and refined room-label scope. Reduces false positives in the room-detection pipeline and improves the quantity output that feeds az-takeoff.

prep.what: Upgrade the takeoff engine’s text classification to distinguish outlined firm names, callout annotations, and room labels — the M3 label lane that reduces false rooms and cleans up quantity output.
prep.understand: The M2 label pass treats all text elements similarly, so the engine often picks up firm names in the title block and callout leaders as room labels. This creates false positives: ‘JONES FLOORING’ and ‘2x4 @ 16” O.C.’ show up as rooms. M3 needs three new discriminators: (1) a title-block exclusion zone (text in the border/corner region is a firm name, not a room), (2) leader-line proximity detection (callout labels attach to a leader, not float in open space), (3) refined room-label classification (room labels sit inside a room polygon). Clean label lanes = fewer false rooms = better quantity output from t18.
approach: Find the M2 label detection code — search for `classify`, `label`, or `text_element` in the takeoff-engine repo; this is the module to extend.

Implement title-block exclusion: detect the drawing border rectangle (typically at the page edge/corner); any text inside the border margin zone is a firm name — exclude it from room label candidates.
Implement callout detection: check if a text element is within N pixels of a leader line (diagonal line segment); if so, tag it as a callout, not a room label.
Run the v2 classifier against the existing M2 test blueprints; compare false-positive room count vs M2 baseline and adjust thresholds.
resources: M2 label detection module — search `classify`, `label`, or `text_element` in the takeoff-engine repo
M2 test blueprint fixtures — the same set used to validate M2; reuse for regression comparison
M3 spec or roadmap doc in `docs/` (if it exists) — the vision target this task builds toward
Blueprint title-block geometry — understand how the border/title block is structured in the SVG or rasterized format the engine processes

tasks.notes: Extend the per-room assembly output with the three main interior trade quantities: floor_sf (area), wall_sf (perimeter × wall_height), ceiling_sf (area). Wall height is a configurable default (9ft) with optional per-room override from blueprint annotations or project config. Output feeds az-takeoff’s t45 (wall paint area) and t46 (trade routing) — coordinate field names.

prep.what: Extend the takeoff engine’s per-room assembly output with paint, drywall, and flooring quantities derived from room geometry plus wall height — the measurement layer az-takeoff’s trade pricing depends on.
prep.understand: Currently the engine outputs `floor_sf` (area) per room. That’s it. Painting and drywall need `wall_sf = perimeter × wall_height`. Ceiling work needs `ceiling_sf = area`. Wall height doesn’t exist in a 2D blueprint — it must be a configurable default (9ft residential standard) with optional per-room override via blueprint annotation parsing if the drawing marks ceiling height, otherwise manual in the project config. The output of this task is the assembly object per room that az-takeoff’s t45 will consume this afternoon. Coordinate the field names now: az-takeoff expects something like `wall_paint_sf` or `wall_sf` — confirm before you emit.
approach: Find the current per-room assembly computation — search for `floor_sf`, `area`, or `assembly` in the takeoff-engine codebase; this is the object to extend.

Add `wall_height` to the engine’s project/room config: default 9.0, overridable per room. Check if any blueprint annotation (e.g. ‘CLG HT: 9-0’) can be parsed from the label pass (t26 just cleaned up); if so, wire it.
Compute and emit: `floor_sf = room.area`, `wall_sf = room.perimeter * wall_height`, `ceiling_sf = room.area`. Add these to the assembly object output.
Update the `GET /assemblies` (or equivalent) API response to include the new fields. Write a quick test: 10×10 room, height=9 → floor=100, wall=360, ceiling=100.
resources: Per-room assembly code — search `floor_sf`, `area`, or `assembly` in the takeoff-engine repo
`GET /assemblies` or `GET /rooms` endpoint — where the output is exposed; check any OpenAPI spec if it exists
